major_cooldowns.name: Tranquility
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Ramp into it: land as many Rejuvenations as you can plus a Wild Growth, then channel it on the fight's heaviest damage and chain Regrowth through the 10 second heal-over-time extension it leaves behind.
major_cooldowns.id_note: 740 is the cast id; 157982 shares the name and is not the pressed button.

major_cooldowns.name: Convoke the Spirits
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Send it often on the most dangerous moments, with Rejuvenations already out so its 45% chance to extend every heal-over-time effect by 2 seconds has something to extend, and press Nature's Swiftness first to buff the Regrowths it rolls without consuming the buff.
major_cooldowns.id_note: Choice node opposite Incarnation: Tree of Life.

major_cooldowns.name: Incarnation: Tree of Life
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Take it for long healing phases such as a 30 second burn, press it before a Rejuvenation ramp so those casts are cheap, and keep Wild Growth and free-cast Regrowth flowing so you are actively healing for the whole window.
major_cooldowns.id_note: Choice node opposite Convoke the Spirits; not pressed in the sampled parse.

major_cooldowns.name: Innervate
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Self-cast it starting around 80% mana and fit as many into the fight as you can, lining the 8 free seconds up with a Rejuvenation ramp rather than Regrowth, which Abundance already makes cheap.

major_cooldowns.name: Nature's Swiftness
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Spend it on an instant, 60% stronger Regrowth to save someone dropping low, or press it just before Convoke the Spirits to buff every Regrowth the channel rolls since Convoke does not consume it.
major_cooldowns.id_note: 132158 is the Druid cast; 378081 shares the name and is the Shaman version.

major_cooldowns.name: Ironbark
major_cooldowns.usage_rule: Drop the 20% damage reduction on anyone about to take heavy damage; it is off the global cooldown and comes back fast, so using it often beats saving it for a perfect moment.
major_cooldowns.id_note: Not pressed in the sampled parse but a real castable ability.

defensives.name: Barkskin
defensives.usage_rule: Your personal 20% damage reduction on a short cooldown: press it any time you are in danger, and note it also stops damage from pushing back your casts.

defensives.name: Survival Instincts
defensives.usage_rule: Save the 50% reduction for a hit Barkskin cannot cover.
defensives.id_note: Not pressed in the sampled parse but a real castable ability.

defensives.name: Frenzied Regeneration
defensives.usage_rule: Shift to Bear and heal 24% of your health over 3 seconds when sustained damage is on you and you cannot spare casts on yourself.
defensives.id_note: Requires Bear Form and 10 Rage; only 1 application in the sampled parse.

rules.action: Swiftmend on cooldown and follow it with Rejuvenation: Soul of the Forest plus Power of the Archdruid put that Rejuvenation on 3 targets. Follow with Regrowth instead only when the group is already struggling to stay alive.

Keep Lifebloom on yourself at all times in raid: you stack healing modifiers on yourself, so your Everbloom bloom is far larger, and Lifetreading parks Efflorescence under your own feet. In dungeons put it on the tank or whoever is taking heavy damage.
Keep Efflorescence down under a clump of players for its full 30 seconds, and have it and Lifebloom up before a known damage event lands.

Press your first Innervate around 80% mana and keep using it every cooldown. Sitting on it until you are empty costs you whole casts of it over a fight, and most mana problems are that plus too few Regrowths.
Follow Nature's Swiftness with Regrowth on the target that dropped low: it is instant and heals 60% more. Keep casting Regrowth on them until they are safe.

rules.description: Wild Growth into the Tranquility ramp
rules.action: Plan the Tranquility ramp before the fight: get 12 or more Rejuvenations out in raid, 3 to 5 in a key, plus a Wild Growth, then channel Tranquility so all of it is extended by 10 seconds and your follow-up Regrowths cost nothing at max Abundance.

rules.description: Nature's Swiftness before Convoke the Spirits
rules.action: When Nature's Swiftness is up, press it right before Convoke the Spirits. Convoke does not consume the buff, so every Regrowth it rolls heals 60% more.

source_summary: Restoration Druid healing is heal-over-time maintenance plus the Abundance cycle: keep Lifebloom on yourself and Efflorescence under the group, Swiftmend on cooldown into Rejuvenation, Wild Growth often, then chain Regrowth while Rejuvenation stacks are high. The big cooldowns are ramp tools rather than panic buttons: build a wide Rejuvenation and Wild Growth carpet before Tranquility so its 10 second extension and Convoke the Spirits' 2 second extensions hold the ramp open, and pick Convoke or Incarnation: Tree of Life for the fight's damage pattern. Innervate starts around 80% mana and is used every cooldown into Rejuvenation casts, Nature's Swiftness answers spike damage with an instant Regrowth or pre-buffs Convoke, and Ironbark goes out often rather than being saved.
